title: Longest substring without repeating characters
prompt:
PageTurn records which book a student opened in each session as one character per session. A "focus streak" is a run of consecutive sessions with no character repeated.

Write lengthOfLongestUnique(text) that returns the length of the longest substring of text with no repeated characters. Aim for O(n) time.

Examples:

  • lengthOfLongestUnique("ABCBDAE") → 5 ("CBDAE")
  • lengthOfLongestUnique("abcabcbb") → 3 ("abc")
  • lengthOfLongestUnique("bbbbb") → 1
  • lengthOfLongestUnique("pwwkew") → 3 ("wke"; "pwke" is not contiguous)

Constraints: 0 ≤ text.length ≤ 5 × 104; any characters, including spaces and digits. Characters are case-sensitive.

tests.name: the left edge never moves backward
matches checking every substring on many small inputs

hints: "Longest substring such that a rule holds" is a variable sliding window. The rule here: no character appears twice inside the window.

Keep a Set of the characters in the window text[left..right]. For each new right: while the set already has text[right], remove text[left] and move left forward. Then add text[right] and record right - left + 1.

Shape:

const inWindow = new Set();
let left = 0, best = 0;
for (let right = 0; right < text.length; right++) {
  while (inWindow.has(text[right])) {
    inWindow.delete(text[left]);
    left++;
  }
  inWindow.add(text[right]);
  best = Math.max(best, right - left + 1);
}
return best;
explain:
Time O(n), space O(k) where k is the number of distinct characters (bounded by the alphabet). Each character enters the set once and leaves at most once. Checking every substring is O(n²) or worse.

If you used a Map of last-seen indexes and jumped left to lastIndex + 1, the "abba" test is the trap: you must use Math.max(left, lastIndex + 1) so the left edge never moves backward.

In an interview: "Longest contiguous substring with a rule, so a sliding window. I expand right, keep a set of characters in the window, and shrink from the left while there's a duplicate. Every character enters and leaves once: O(n) time, O(k) space."
